newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar weak on mixed sales, arb steady.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar weak on mixed sales, arb steady.

text.p: Steady mixed selling dragged white sugar futures off the morning's highs in modest turnover and the spot white premium managed to keep pace with the weaker raws market, traders said on Thursday.
Continued buying by one leading trade house throughout the day was not enough to outpace the wealth of sellers determined to drag March lower, they said.
"The London market is doing better than New York on the premium basis...but it's very quiet," said one trader.
Producer selling on the raws market brought New York's equivalent March contract back into a trading range which local traders said was unlikely to inspire new buying.
By 1704 GMT volume on London's whites market amounted to 1,077 lots, which traders said was encouraging for the run up to Europe's Christmas holiday period, although it was gently boosted by crosses.
The market's two front spreads narrowed to even money although the market has yet to revert to a contango situation before the December 1997 contract.
March was down $3.10 at $304.50, the same value as May which was $2.60 lower on the day.
Some news emerged on this week's Iraqi buying tender as Jordanian traders said Iraq was still evaluating more than 120 offers from international suppliers.
But a final decision mayu not be taken before early next week as the extent of Iraqi puchases will depend on prices.
Paris trading was confined to the two nearby Matif contracts. March and May were both $2.00 lower at $304.50 and total volume was 766 lots. -- Jeremy Smith, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8064
